title: Tenant-safe ID translation & correlation propagation for log ingestion pipeline
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Incoming frontend and runtime logs use a mix of headers (x-request-id, traceparent, x-correlation-id) and opaque tenant IDs. Our Loki/ELK ingest adapters currently write raw values into per-tenant indexes which can leak or collide when requests are proxied or when third-party agents rewrite IDs. We need a deterministic, auditable translation layer that normalizes correlation identifiers, enforces tenant scoping, and emits stable structured fields for downstream dashboards and traces.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware ID translation and propagation module within the ingest adapter that: 1) normalizes common correlation headers to a canonical field (correlation_id), 2) derives a stable global correlation token when upstream IDs are missing, 3) maintains a translation ledger (mapping of original_id -> canonical_id with short TTL) for debugging, and 4) ensures no tenant boundaries are crossed when translating or correlating requests. The pipeline must be compatible with Loki label limits and ES index mappings and provide an opt-in audit log for security reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest adapter emits a canonical field 'correlation_id' for all structured logs (JSON) and a header for legacy flows.

When multiple IDs are present, the adapter follows deterministic precedence (traceparent > x-request-id > x-correlation-id > generated) and records the original values in 'correlation_originals' for 72h.
Tenant scoping enforced: canonical correlation IDs are namespaced per-tenant so queries cannot accidentally correlate across tenants.
Translation ledger is queryable by infra/SEC with RBAC and writes to an encrypted audit stream (S3/HSM-backed) when enabled.
Loki labels and ES mappings validated: no dynamic label explosion; field sizes capped and truncated with reason codes.
E2E test demonstrating correlation propagation from HTTP ingress -> service mesh -> runtime -> Loki/ELK with preserved canonical_id and trace links.
Performance impact measured: <5% p50 latency increase on ingestion pipeline at 95th percentile traffic profile used in benchmarks.
tasks: Design translation algorithm and precedence table for incoming headers
Prototype in ingest-adapter v2: header normalization + ledger write
Add tenant namespace enforcement and TTL semantics for ledger entries
Update Loki/ES emitters to use canonical 'correlation_id' field and store originals as 'correlation_originals' (array)
Add config flags: enable_audit_stream (bool), ledger_ttl_hours (int), tenant_namespace_mode (strict|lenient)
Create E2E harness and synthetic load test to measure latency regressions
Write docs (Console observability guide) and run security review with SEC team
Ship feature flag gated rollout and monitor dashboards for error/latency regressions
notes: Design trade-offs: Storing full originals increases storage; to balance, we TTL originals for 72h and truncate IDs > 256 chars with metadata explaining truncation.
We considered global canonical IDs shared across tenants but rejected due to tenant isolation and compliance concerns.
Implementation will use existing tenant ID from auth token when available; when absent, fallback to source IP + agent-fingerprint hashing to avoid POI collisions.
Loki constraints: dynamic label cardinality is dangerous—we emit correlation_id as a log field and only surface it as a label for authorized debug queries via the Console (controlled by role).
Conformance: add a schema migration doc for Elasticsearch index templates to include 'correlation_id' as keyword and 'correlation_originals' as nested text (with limits).
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-adapter/pull/601 (draft) — prototype code for header normalization and ledger writes.
